utterance: The `storefront-vpc` VPC already carries public traffic, but nothing serves it yet. Bring up a web server in one of the VPC's public subnets and give it a security group that accepts HTTP on port 80 from the load balancer. Then put an internet-facing Application Load Balancer in front of it, spanning the VPC's public subnets, with a security group that accepts HTTP on port 80 from anywhere. The load balancer needs an HTTP listener on port 80 whose default action forwards to a new HTTP target group on port 80 in that VPC that takes instance targets, and that new web server is what should end up registered in that group.

main.responsibility: owns the application's resources and their configuration
main.intent: the storefront-vpc VPC holds a new internet-facing application load balancer spanning at least two of the VPC's public subnets in distinct availability zones and carrying a security group that admits TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0; that load balancer has an HTTP listener on port 80 whose default action forwards to a new target group of instance target type on HTTP port 80 in that VPC; and a new running EC2 instance sits in one of the VPC's public subnets in a security group that admits TCP port 80 from the load balancer's group and is registered as a target of that target group
